newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise as bond rates fall on weak jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise as bond rates fall on weak jobs data.

text.p: Stocks rose sharply Friday as long-term bond interest rates tumbled after a surprisingly weak jobs report and as technology shares rebounded.

At 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average was up 43.49 at 6.816.55, after soaring more than 95 points earlier. The New York Stock Exchange's curbs on index-arbitrage trades were triggered soon after the market opened.
The bellwether 30-year Treasury bond rose nearly three-quarters of a point, reducing its yield to 6.73 percent from 6.76 percent. The yield and the price move in opposite directions.
In the broader market, advances led declining issues by 14 to eight on volume of about 293 million shares on the NYSE.
The Nasdaq Composite index, heavily weighted with high tech issues, was up 7.66 points at 1.354.06.

"The bond market has been under so much pressure that it took the data as an excuse for a relief rally," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "This gave fund managers who are drowning in cash an excuse to buy stocks. Of course, they will chase the big name, high-liquidity stocks as the only place they can put their money to work quickly."

Blumberg said technology stocks were in vogue again after investors' fling with consumer stocks that lasted two or three days. "This seems to be about the average attention span of a portfolio manager," he said.

U.S. non-farm payrolls came in with a higher-than-forecast rise of 271,000 compared with a revised 261,000 the previous month, but analysts said the number had been inflated due to seasonal factors. More importantly, average hourly earnings rose by a mere 1 cent after a sharper rise over the previous two months.
The data, analysts said, eased fears of interest rate tightening any time soon by the Federal Reserve.

High technology stocks drew encouragement from bullish comments made about Intel Corp. by Hambrecht & Quist analyst Rob Chaplinsky who reiterated his buy rating on the stock, saying the company's prospects for earnings growth and multiple expansion remain strong.
Intel was up 3-1/4 at 156-3/8 and Microsoft Corp. was up 2-3/8 at 99-1/2.
Dow component International Business Machines Corp. was up 2-1/8 at 147-3/4.

The loser among the techs was 3Com Corp., the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, down 3-1/4 at 49. Oppenheimer & Co. cut its rating on the stock to market perform from buy and Cowen & Co. cut its rating to buy from strong buy.
Banking stocks followed through on their recent strength, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's bank index up 7.37 points, or 1.26 percent, at 593.90.
Citicorp was up 1-5/8 at 118-1/4 and Chase Manhattan Corp. rose 1-3/4 to 96-3/4.

Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd., said the bank index had risen 10 percent from the start of the year through Friday, only exceeded by the Semiconductor Index, which he said had risen 14 percent through Thursday.
CVS Corp. stock was up 1-7/8 at 45-7/8 and Revco D.S. Inc. was up 2-1/2 at 40-1/2.
The companies said Friday they had definitively agreed for CVS to acquire Revco in a stock transaction valued at about $2.8 billion, plus the assumption of $900 million in Revco debt.
